correctness.rationale: Write μ_j and S_j for the attachment-weighted empirical depth mean and variance. The update μ_j−μ_{j−1}=p_j(1+ξ_j) gives the stated coefficient 1+(n−j)p_j in the centered path length. The empirical variance updates to (1−p_j)S_{j−1}+p_j(1−p_j)(D_j−μ_{j−1})², giving the stated recurrence on taking expectations, since the squared term conditionally has mean 1+S_{j−1}. Orthogonality and fixed-prefix lower bounds give scaled variance divergence when Q=∞. When Q is finite, the recurrence gives bounded v_j if the summed inputs p_j(1−p_j) are finite; otherwise v_j eventually exceeds 1, so ∑p_j² is finite and v_j=O(sqrt(j)). Thus ∑v_j/j² is finite; the two martingale series and Kronecker's lemma dispose of the two remainders almost surely, and orthogonality/dominated convergence dispose of them in L². The recurrence barriers give the subcritical local constant 1/c and the balanced one c/(c²+1/2); beyond 1/2 the summed drift loss is lower order than the accumulated input. Multiplying each v_j by p_j² and summing with (1−j/n)² yields the three beta constants, the logarithmic coefficient at 2/3, and Q beyond it. No assertion of necessity for almost-sure convergence alone is made. /workspace/review_checks/check_1.py independently compares exact seven-vertex moments for three schedules; it does not prove the limits.
